# lakekeeper_generic_table_protection (Resource)

The `lakekeeper_generic_table_protection` resource manages the protection flag of one generic table in Lakekeeper.

Protection prevents Lakekeeper from dropping the generic table. The generic table itself is not managed by this resource: create it with an Iceberg or Generic Table client and reference its ID here.

Changing `protected` sets or clears the flag. **Destroying this resource only removes it from Terraform state; it does not change the protection flag on the server.** Unprotect the generic table explicitly with `protected = false` before removing the resource if that is what you want.

Changing `warehouse_id` or `generic_table_id` also only removes the old resource from Terraform state: it does not change the protection flag of the generic table it referred to, so a protected generic table stays protected. Add a `lakekeeper_generic_table_protection` block for that generic table with `protected = false` to unprotect it.

A missing or soft-deleted generic table cannot be protected: Lakekeeper rejects the request and the provider reports the error instead of silently skipping the change.

**Upstream API**: [Lakekeeper REST API docs](https://docs.lakekeeper.io/docs/nightly/api/management/#tag/warehouse/operation/set_generic_table_protection)

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The generic table is created outside Terraform; reference its existing UUID.
resource "lakekeeper_generic_table_protection" "images" {
  warehouse_id     = "a4653498-1dd9-4f12-a2e4-1cc7d4023226"
  generic_table_id = "2b7d4f3a-8c1e-4a5b-9f0d-1e2a3b4c5d6e"
  protected        = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `generic_table_id` (String) The ID of the generic table.
- `protected` (Boolean) Whether the generic table is protected from deletion.
- `warehouse_id` (String) The ID of the warehouse that contains the generic table.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The internal ID of this resource, in the form `{{warehouse_id}}/{{generic_table_id}}`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# id is "{{warehouse_id}}/{{generic_table_id}}"
terraform import lakekeeper_generic_table_protection.images "a4653498-1dd9-4f12-a2e4-1cc7d4023226/2b7d4f3a-8c1e-4a5b-9f0d-1e2a3b4c5d6e"
```
